evidence_quotes: Four of the 12 events carried tsunami flags
all three recorded events at depths of 8.7 km or less with tsunami flags active

The M5.7 at 55 km E of Kermadec Islands (2026-02-08, depth 5.7 km), the M5.5 in the New Britain region, PNG (2026-02-03, depth 7.4 km), and the M5.5 at 30 km E of Tual, Indonesia (2026-01-27, depth 5.4 km) all returned tsunami = true
The dataset covers a 31-day window from 2026-01-17 to 2026-02-16
criticisms: The Risk Watch section states 'all three recorded events at depths of 8.7 km or less with tsunami flags active' — but the Kermadec Islands event is at 5.7 km, New Britain/PNG at 7.4 km, and Tual/Indonesia at 5.4 km. The 8.7 km figure belongs to the Mohr, Iran event, which did NOT have a tsunami flag. This conflates the Iran depth with the tsunami-flagged events, creating a false metadata association.

The report counts 4 tsunami-flagged events in the Executive Summary, but only names 3 in the Top Signals bullet (Kermadec Islands, New Britain/PNG, Tual/Indonesia). The fourth tsunami-flagged event is not identified anywhere in the report. The digest shows the Tual, Indonesia event (2026-01-27) as tsunami=true, New Britain PNG (2026-02-03) as tsunami=true, and Kermadec Islands (2026-02-08) as tsunami=true — that is only 3 events with tsunami=true in the sample. The report claims 4 tsunami flags but the digest sample only shows 3 tsunami=true events, making the count of 4 unverifiable from the provided sample_events.
The date range from 2026-01-17 to 2026-02-16 is 30 days, not 31 days as stated in the Data Caveats section ('31-day window').
